facts.fact: Russia is home to Lake Baikal, which holds about 20% of the world's unfrozen fresh water and is so clear you can see 130 feet down.
facts.flagElement: the deep blue wavy stripe representing Lake Baikal

facts.fact: The Trans-Siberian Railway spans 9,289 kilometers across eight time zones, making it the longest continuous railway line on Earth.
facts.flagElement: the horizontal black railroad track stripe crossing the flag

facts.fact: Russia has more brown bears than any other country in the world, with an estimated 120,000 living in its vast forests and tundra.
facts.flagElement: the brown triangular mountain shape pointing upward

decoys.overlap: Good thinking — Canada does have vast forests full of brown bears and impressive wilderness. But it doesn't have the world's longest railway line or that record-breaking freshwater lake.

Solid guess — Mongolia does border that famous deep freshwater lake and has extensive railway connections from its Soviet past. But it's not known for having massive bear populations in the way this flag suggests.

Understandable choice — Finland does have significant brown bear populations in its northern forests and countless lakes. However, it has no transcontinental railway system stretching across multiple time zones.
